title: Mykola Azarov

fields.label: Position held
fields.value: Prime Minister of Ukraine, Prime Minister of Ukraine

summary: Mykola Yanovych Azarov is a notable Russo-Ukrainian politician who served as the [[prime-minister-of-ukraine|Prime Minister of Ukraine]] from 11 March 2010 to 27 January 2014. His political career is marked by significant roles in the [[cabinet-of-ministers-of-ukraine|Ukrainian government]] and his controversial actions during the Euromaidan protests.

sections.heading: Early Life and Education
paragraphs: Mykola Azarov was born on 17 December 1947 in Kaluga, Russian SFSR, [[soviet-union|Soviet Union]], to a father of half-Russian and half-Estonian descent and a Russian mother. He adopted his wife's surname upon marriage. Azarov attended Moscow State University, where he earned a doctorate in geology and mineralogy in 1973. He worked at the Tulaugol coal enterprise until 1976 and moved to [[donetsk|Donetsk]] in 1984, where he became deputy director of the [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] State Geological Institute.

sections.heading: Political Career
paragraphs: Azarov began his political career in 1994 when he was elected to the [[verkhovna-rada|Verkhovna Rada]], representing the Petroskiy electoral district in Donetsk. He served as head of the parliament's Committee on Budgets from 1995 to 1997 and was involved in supporting then-President [[leonid-kuchma|Leonid Kuchma]]. He was appointed Chairman of the State Tax Administration of [[ukraine|Ukraine]] in 1996, a position he held until 2002, during which time he faced allegations of using his role to influence political outcomes.

In 2002, Azarov became First Vice Prime Minister and Finance Minister, implementing economic reforms that contributed to significant GDP growth [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]]. He served as acting prime minister during political transitions in 2004 and later became a prominent figure in the Party of Regions.

sections.heading: Prime Ministership
paragraphs: Following [[viktor-yanukovych|Viktor Yanukovych]]'s election as [[president-of-ukraine|President of Ukraine]], Azarov was appointed Prime Minister on 11 March 2010, with 242 votes in favor from the Verkhovna Rada. He was re-elected to parliament in the 2012 elections and continued to serve as Prime Minister until his resignation on 28 January 2014 amid the [[euromaidan|Euromaidan]] protests. His resignation was aimed at facilitating a peaceful resolution to the conflict.

After resigning, Azarov fled to Russia and claimed to have been offered political refugee status by [[vladimir-putin|Vladimir Putin]]. He has since been on the international wanted list for alleged abuse of power and is subject to sanctions from multiple countries.

sections.heading: Post-Resignation Activities
paragraphs: In August 2015, Azarov announced the formation of the Ukraine Salvation Committee, a government in exile that sought to unify various political factions to restore order in Ukraine. He has been involved in controversial activities and statements regarding Ukraine's political landscape since his departure.

sections.heading: Cultural and Political Image
paragraphs: Azarov's command of the Ukrainian language has been criticized, and he has been labeled the most Russophile member of his cabinet. His comments on gender roles in government and corruption have sparked backlash and legal actions from women's rights groups in Ukraine. He has expressed views on historical events that have been contentious in the context of Ukrainian national identity.
